parsed.prompt_text: Which sport do you like to play or watch most? Please describe it.
suggested_ideas: name of the sport
where you usually play or watch it
what you do in the sport

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one sport and gives a short personal description of it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear sport choice; at least one detail about playing or watching the sport.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common or less common sport is acceptable. The student may talk about playing, watching, or both. Short simple answers are acceptable if they stay on the topic.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking mainly about school subjects, food, a famous person without mentioning the sport choice, or a general talk about exercise with no sport named.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For pronunciation, listen for clear individual words, especially the sport name and common simple sentences. Minor grammar errors are fine if words are understandable. A very short but clear response can still be acceptable.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a sport clearly; giving only one word with no support; mispronouncing key words so the sport is hard to identify; going off topic to talk about unrelated hobbies.

parsed.prompt_text: What sport do you like best? Give one example and say one reason you like it.
suggested_ideas: name one sport you like such as football, badminton, running, or swimming
say a simple reason such as fun, healthy, relaxing, or playing with friends
use short simple sentences

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one sport, gives one example, and says one simple reason for liking it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear choice of one sport; one example sport; one easy reason.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common sport is acceptable. The student may answer with a familiar sport from school or daily life. Very simple language is acceptable.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about a famous athlete, listing many sports without choosing one, or speaking about games or music instead of sports.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on intelligibility of short connected speech. Check whether key words such as the sport name, like, and because are pronounced clearly enough to understand.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a sport clearly; giving no reason; listing too many ideas; unclear pronunciation of the sport name or key reason words.

parsed.prompt_text: If you can choose one sport for your free time this week, what will you choose? Say what you need and why it is a good choice for you.
suggested_ideas: name the sport
say simple things you need, for example a ball, a racket, or open space
say why it is good for your free time this week

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker chooses one sport for the near future, mentions simple things needed for it, and gives a personal reason.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear sport choice; one or two basic items or conditions needed; a simple reason such as fun, healthy, relaxing, or suitable for free time.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any simple sport is acceptable, including football, badminton, basketball, volleyball, table tennis, swimming, or skipping rope. Students may answer with simple future meaning even if grammar is not perfect.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking about a full weekly schedule without choosing a sport, discussing shopping plans in detail, or describing a holiday activity unrelated to sports.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Judge pronunciation by how clearly the student says the chosen sport, needed items, and short reason. Simple words said clearly should score better than longer unclear sentences.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Forgetting to mention what is needed; choosing an activity that is not clearly a sport; listing many objects without a reason; pronunciation that makes key nouns hard to understand.

parsed.prompt_text: Some students like team sports and some like individual sports. Which do you prefer for your free time, and why? Give one example sport and say what you need to play it.
suggested_ideas: say whether you prefer team sports or individual sports
give one example, such as football, badminton, or swimming
say one or two things you need and why this choice is good for your free time

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker states a preference between team sports and individual sports, gives one example sport, mentions simple things needed for it, and gives a personal reason.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear preference; one example sport; one or two basic items or conditions needed; a simple reason such as fun, healthy, relaxing, or easy to do in free time.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any simple sport is acceptable, including football, badminton, basketball, volleyball, table tennis, swimming, running, or skipping rope. Students may use simple language and do not need to make a long comparison.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about school subjects, giving a shopping list without naming a sport, or discussing an activity that is not clearly a sport.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Judge pronunciation by how clearly the student says the preference, the sport name, the needed items, and the reason. Clear key words are more important than complex sentences.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not stating a preference between the two types of sport; forgetting to give an example sport; forgetting to mention what is needed; pronunciation that makes the sport name or reason hard to understand.
